question.problem: Given that ${a}_{1}=-\frac{5}{2}$ and $\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}=-\frac{1}{10}$ for all integers $n\ge 1,$ find the value of ${\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the given series is geometric series because the ratio of any two consecutive terms is constant.

The sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of a geometric series is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r},\,|r|<1,
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term and $r$ is the common ratio.

We're told that the first term is

$$
{a}_{1}=-\frac{5}{2}.
$$

The common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}=-\frac{1}{10}.
$$

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{5}{2}}{(1-(-\frac{1}{10}))} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{5}{2}}{(\frac{11}{10})} \\  & =-\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{10}{11} \\  & =-\frac{25}{11}\end{aligned}
$$
